findings.title: Chunked-Encoding chunk terminator is discarded without validating CRLF
findings.evidence: ChunkedReader never checks the 2-byte chunk terminator. After finishing a chunk it sets self._bytes_to_discard = 2 (line 197); on the next call the branch at lines 163-167 calls buf.maybe_extract_at_most(self._bytes_to_discard) and subtracts the consumed count (line 167), discarding whatever 2 bytes arrive without verifying they are CRLF. Reachability: an attacker-controlled request/response with 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' selects ChunkedReader through _body_framing/_get_io_object in _connection.py, and the attacker's bytes flow from Connection.receive_data() into ReceiveBuffer and then into this reader via next_event(). A body such as '5 CRLF AAAAA XX 2 CRLF 45 CRLF 0 CRLF CRLF GET /two ...' is accepted because 'XX' is blindly discarded and parsing continues to the next chunk. A front-end proxy whose chunk parser instead consumes trailing bytes up to the next CRLF (the pound-style bug described in the advisory) interprets the identical byte stream as a single request, so the two HTTP processors disagree on message boundaries, enabling HTTP request smuggling (CWE-444). This is GHSA-vqfr-h8mv-ghfj / CVE-2025-43859 (CVSS 3.1 9.1); it is fixed in h11 0.16.0 by storing the literal b'\r\n' in _bytes_to_discard and raising LocalProtocolError when the consumed bytes do not match. Exploitation requires a co-deployed proxy/parser with a differing chunk-terminator bug (the advisory calls the leniency harmless on its own), but the unsafe operation -- accepting arbitrary framing bytes as the chunk terminator -- is entirely within this reader.
